title: Are We All Pretending To Have Money? | The Buy Now, Pay Later Scam
summary: Personal finance/culture essay video arguing BNPL is part of a broader culture of casual debt and overconsumption in America.

assertions.quote: in most cases, buy now pay later platforms don't report timely payments to credit bureaus, meaning that you don't build credit

verdicts.note: True of Klarna and Afterpay historically, but Affirm already reports and scoring models are being built to incorporate the data.
CFPB: lenders do not typically report BNPL loans to nationwide consumer reporting companies.
Fed SHED: at the time of the survey, most BNPL providers were not reporting loans to credit bureaus, and even reported loans did not factor into scores.

KC Fed endnote: a good repayment record on credit cards improves a consumer's score, while a BNPL repayment record often doesn't, since most BNPL providers don't report repayment behavior to credit bureaus.

CFPB: BNPL lenders 'historically have not furnished loan performance data to the credit bureaus,' consistent with on-time repayment usually not building a user's credit history the way a credit card does.

assertions.quote: if your debt gets sent to collections, your score can tank

verdicts.note: Missed payments and charge-offs sent to collections routinely appear on credit reports and lower scores.

KC Fed: unlike credit cards, a single missed or late BNPL repayment may not lower a consumer's score by itself; the score is hurt only once unrepaid loans are turned over to debt collectors, who do report to bureaus.

assertions.quote: consumer use of buy now pay later apps for things like groceries, which are a necessity
41% of buy now pay later users reported paying late in the past year, up from 34% the year before
nearly a quarter of users said they'd had three or more buy now pay later loans active at once

verdicts.note: Federal Reserve and CFPB survey data show most users hold multiple simultaneous loans, with no single lender seeing the full stack.

KC Fed endnote citing CFPB (2025): 63% of BNPL users had simultaneous loans at any firm during 2022, and 33% had simultaneous loans at different firms, consistent with debt being easy to stack and hard to track across apps.

CFPB defines 'loan stacking' as the risk that a borrower takes out concurrent BNPL loans at different lenders who have no visibility into each other's exposure, because BNPL lenders rely on soft-only credit checks and generally don't furnish loan data to the bureaus.

assertions.quote: BNPL is subverting established regulation around consumer loans like credit cards

verdicts.note: This is a dispute about motive and the appropriate regulatory framing, not a factual claim that can be checked against evidence.

CFPB's own finding -- that 'some market participants' offerings appear to be structured to evade certain federal consumer lending requirements' -- corroborates critics' side of this dispute, though the report doesn't document BNPL companies' own stated rationale for different regulatory treatment.

assertions.quote: nearly half of all buy now pay later purchases are clothing and fashion... the pattern is more impulsive
